title: Strength of Every RPG Maker Versions

posts.author: EpicFILE
posts.body:
I hope I posted this in correct section.
Although the newest version already exist (MZ), some prefer to use older versions (like XP, VXA).
That makes me wonder, is there particular strength in each versions?
*From 2k up to MZ.

posts.author: Darth Equus
posts.body: Ace was the pinnacle of Ruby. Also, custom formulas for the first time.

posts.author: RCXGaming
posts.body:
VX Ace's strength is depth of legacy content, both art and scriptwise. MV has a lot of the same, but with the ability to freely customize resolution size, being able to be used on more than just Windows, Javascript being a more versatile programming language, the Yanfly suite of plugins introducing Action Sequences, etc.
XP has a killer RTP sound effect pool, like there's so much in there that just isn't in future engines. Good soundtrack + it actually has a function where animations play differently if the attack misses as opposed to just showing nothing? Plus a lot of the RTP sprites are very nice looking, though you'd have to tweak them a little for future engines.

posts.author: Danatoth
posts.body:
I'd say that XP had some cool tiles but that's about it.  Ace has a ton of plugins and is the start of when "real rpg maker" started. MV is the go to rpg maker with a ton of free plugins, and introduced the most customization options AND introduced Javascript. MZ builds on MV but is gated by a vast majority of plugins requiring hefty price tags.
ACE = The age of origins
MV = The golden age
MZ = The age of commodities

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
EpicFILE said:
That makes me wonder, is there particular strength in each versions?
*From 2k up to MZ.
Click to expand...
yes and no
the main reason why all older makers are still available is that developing a game takes years (sometimes decades if it is only a hobby), and you don't switch engines mid-development.
And after that you need to consider the development history of the makers. I know that not everyone agrees to my interpretation of this, so make your own opinion on it.
XP was the first milestone and the first maker that had script access (all older makers are eventing only), but unfortunately they added too many critical features and the computers of the time when RMXP was modern could often not handle everything it could do - the unlimited tilesets for example easily slowed down even the best computers due to their RAM requirements.
This "feature" (theoretically unlimited tilesets) is still unique to RMXP
But after seeing the performance problems of XP on the common computers of their time I believe that the programmers panicked and then removed most of the critical features from VX. For example they limited the single tileset allowed, removed manual control on layering for mapping and so on.
As a result in my opinion the VX is the worst maker of all.
Then came VXAce, which is probably the second great milestone for several reasons.
Technically that is the introduction of the still current database structure with many new features like multiple tilesets and the already mentioned damage formulae and more.
Outside technical reasons Ace was the first maker ever to be internationally distributed and be placed on Steam - all other makers you currently find on steam were added later retroactively.
MV and MZ switched the internal script language to javascript to allow for porting to other OS and devices - again with mixed results, although none of the problems were in the engine itself which is a simple upgrade from Ace.
The problem of MV was that they advertised it for mobile export (android/iOS) without warning that a mobile device simply doesn't have the computing power of a full computer.
As a result a lot of people expected their games that run easily on full computers do the same on a mobile phone or tablet - which is impossible, you have to limit the scope of your game to the lower computer end for it to work on mobile.
As a result the mobile export was a bit more hidden and no longer advertised on MZ, although it is still available (it is nothing but a wrapper around the www export).
About the other differences between MV and MZ, there are three main ones:
1) MV is the only one with an official Linux version of the editor, and I don't believe they will add a linux version to MZ as it has been too long. Probably didn't sell enough even if some vocal people really liked the Linux version.
2) MZ is the first maker since XP that re-added the manual layer control, the most missed feature since XP and one of the reasons why RMXP was still extremely popular through Ace and MV.
3) MZ is also the engine where many programmers obfuscate and sell their plugins instead of making them available free for non-commercial.
I understand that they want compensation for their work, but the obfuscation made compatibility patches between plugins almost impossible and is one reason why many didn't switch from MV to MZ.
And then we come to RM Unite - which was a disaster in many ways.
In hindsight it is obvious that the programmers thought they need a massive upgrade to get more interest again, and the original feature list for Unite had many good ideas added.
But based on the delays and removed features before releasing something that didn't even run correctly on most purchaser's computers they should have taken one or better two years of additional programming work before even trying to release it.
According to the latest reviews (I decided against purchasing it) they seem to have gotten it stable now, but they also effectively crippled the community for it by demanding that all questions should be redirected to their own forum (which is one reason why it isn't supported here).
A Forum that proudly states on its main site: "A community is a place intended for users to help each other, and Gotcha Gotcha Games does not directly respond to posts."
Does anyone wonder why that forum still has less than 500 posts for the combined english and japanese community?....

posts.author: Prescott
posts.body:
2003 has a really robust event system, or so I've heard. I haven't actually used it all that much. It's also the one that's the most easily compatible with a wide range of devices thanks to the folks working on Easy RPG, which will let you playing 2000/2003 games on pretty much anything from like the Wii onward.
XP had layers going for it, but now that MZ is out that's not really a huge factor anymore. It's got a killer RTP though, dare I say the best in the series. Everything from the battlers to the characters, the tilesets, the music, all awesome.
VX doesn't have any strengths. No real reason to buy it or use it. If I remember right, pretty much everyone stayed on XP up until VX Ace came out, and even then there were people like myself using XP all the way up until MV. When it came out it had a slightly better scripting system, and I think it may have had side view battles also but I'm not sure. It stripped out the layers for the maps though, which a lot of people didn't particularly like.
VX Ace is, like has been mentioned, uses battle formulas and has the final form of RGSS. I'm not sure how much of that was actually realized though because I never used it all that much. I do know that someone got a working full 3D renderer in XP which as far as I ever saw RGSS pushed, but not sure about RGSS3.
MV is one of the best. Switching to a more common language helped it a lot. Then you have 48x48 tiles which increases the possible detail even over VX/VX Ace's 32x32 tiles.
So far, I'd say MZ is easily the definitive version of the engine, with everything good about all of the makers in one and then some. It's still good old RPG Maker at its core yet there is so much extra sauce to it. People will talk about the prohibitive cost of it, and suggest MV instead, and so it goes. If you're a hobbyist then it's probably better to stick with MV, but man it's hard to say no to MZ when it has all the good stuff MV does plus the mapping from XP.
Taking it to a weirder world, the console side of things, I think some of those have merit too. I haven't played FES, but I know a lot of people got into RPG Maker that way. I've played a fair amount of RPG Maker 3 on PS2 as well and I really wish we could get something like that on PC. Imagining a 3D RPG Maker like that where you could import custom models and such would be so awesome. Heck, I imagine even using it with all its limitations on a mouse and keyboard with an actual game exporter would even be fun to use. Not really commercially viable or anything like that, but just for fun. Actually, with how much people yearn for retro style graphics, I can see a brand new 3D RPG Maker coming out with RTP that looks like it was straight out of the PS1 or PS2 still being pretty well liked. RPG Maker 3 is really a fine engine, just stuck on the wrong platform. A few tweaks could go a long way.

posts.author: jonthefox
posts.body:
Sort of, it mostly boils down to MZ being the best engine with the most quality of life features, but MV has a lot of plugins written for it that some people don't want to give up.  And then some people are proficient in some of the programming languages that go with older engines.  Other than that, it comes down to which RTP you find most appealing, has the most resources, or just goes best with your style of game - though there are ways to get most resources compatible with MZ.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
I live and die by XP. Part of that is probably that I'm a grumpy old lady who resists changes in my hobbies, but mostly it's because the art style and the tools available in it really, really appeal to me. It also doesn't hurt that the RTP is really, really robust--I don't know if it's actually larger than later engines' default resource pool, but it sure feels that way.
I don't like the single-tile-tall, super-chibi characters that later engines use--XP is built to handle taller characters, and that means things like the passability settings of tilesets are better suited to them. I love the art style of XP. I love the crispness of the pixel art, and find that "painted" tiles sort of tend to look...unclear by comparison? It's like looking at a slightly out-of-focus photo. It's very pretty, but you can't quite make out the details.
I steadfastly refused to give up manual mapping layers, so I even though I had VX/A and MV, I never gave any serious thought to switching until MZ--and even though MZ had manual mapping layers, I
also
didn't want to have to rebuild my entire resource collection in 48px, so I didn't actually do anything with MZ until it got the update to change the tile size.
I also don't care for the "tabbed" tileset approach or autotile-based mapping. Autotiles are cool and everything, but using them as heavily as newer engines does felt a little
too
"auto" for my tastes. The only thing I've done with MZ is enter a mapping contest, and in that short project my most-used phrase was "please stop changing my walls just because I flood-filled the floor with a different color tile." Drove me crazy, and I went straight back to XP when I was done XD
So that's my little soapbox rant about why I still use XP. I'm not trying to prove anything objectively right or wrong, I just still really enjoy it.

posts.author: Akkari
posts.body:
Alot of people seem to forget to mention this with 2k3 and write it off as some old software so I'm gonna add to this so it gets some light lol
RM2k3 if used with easyrpg player is the most compatible version of RPG Maker, as already mentioned above(on windows, literally allows you to play most games(definitely any base/non-patched games) from 98-11 smoothly). So multiplatform is possible with 2k3.
Then there's maniacs patch, which greatly expands the already extensive eventing system and allows you to do some coding(so the argument that you can't code in a RM2k3 isn't actually strictly true and there should always be an asterisk above that statement). Tbh with maniacs patch, RM2k3 kinda goes above most of the other engines when you just look at features and what can be done with eventing alone, also I feel like RM2k3 has best looking games(I'm not just talking about graphics here) as well as the craziest projects that people have done.
The only downsides I can think of that might turn people away is the 8bit image requirement, limited layers for tiles, 16x16 tiles when you prefer to work with larger tile sizes(although this and layers could possibly be worked around using Maniacs Picture Sprite sheets) and the editor UI being a bit dated(although the modern editors are literally the same with a fresher coat of paint and a few QOL improvements). There's also the issue of very little tutorials and documentation other than the built in manual for 2k3, especially for maniacs which has it's documentation in Japanese only plus one in depth guide which only has some of it translated into English.
TL;DR: I might not recommend it to most people, but imo RM2k3 is alot more powerful and viable than most people say and most stuff people say it doesn't have or can't do is available via maniacs or EasyRPG and so should not be written off so easily.

posts.author: Lord Vectra
posts.body:
I will only speak on what I own which is XP, VX, VXA, and MV (not worth the bucks to upgrade to MZ). I will mention RTPs though they're kind of moot to me because I use whatever RTP of these I want for a project and just edit them to fit into whatever style I'm going for.
XP (My current game proj choice) - For me, ruby scripting is easy for me, and I recently found out about the technically infinite tilesets. At first, I thought the lack of autotile was bothering me, but when I booted up VXA again, I realized it wasn't that autotile was gone but that XP's RTP tilesets just don't have a lot individually (imo, they're bad unless you combine them). I started combining them, and now I'm happy. The RTP battlers are pretty dated and some are downright ugly. RTP Tilesets and characters are both good which is mainly because there is an appeal to have non-chibis so XP is the only one with non-chibi RTPs with tilesets to support that. Of course, it also has a lot of legacy support and still suprisingly gets scripting support albeit nowhere near as much as it used to.
RTP animations are ok (dated but retro games are in the market). You can't combine 2 like you can with future installations, so you gotta treat them like tilesets and get to combining. It does have unique mechanics like having animations sound/look different based on hit/misses.
I personally find the default battle system better and thus easier to build from. That also had built-in features like caster and target animations which you would still need scripts for in future installations.
I'm using it for my current project becausee I prefer XP's default battle system as a foundation. There is nothing I want in my project that XP would be unable to do. Another major reason is I'm using a Mode7 3D script that I can't find a good replication in VXA, and I like the flavor it adds.
VX - Believe Andar. It was not good imo. I almost feel like saying its a downgrade from XP is an understatement. Funny enough, this is actually what I started with, but man, when I moved to VXA, it was a breath of fresh air.
VXA - I used this the most in my hobbying. Best database that is also ruby (important distinction). Many more built-in functions of multi-hits, weapon requirements, etc. Was quite the massive upgrade and while it didn't have multi-layers, there were workarounds by using events which isn't the best but sufficed for many people's needs, including my own. I should also mention they added new event methods which is great. RTP Iconset is amazing, tilesets are nice if you don't mind chibis, and characters are ok. it has a character and face creator though the face creator is pretty hot garbage.
RTP Battlers are obviously more polished with much higher contrast (too much imo). No longer blocky and ugly like some of XP's battlers.
Default battle system is a downgrade imo and is very much barebones but nothing scripts can't fix (you will most likely want a script though).
The strength is surely in the database though. There were times I contemplated starting from scratch simply because VXA handles status effect inflictions SO much better (I don't know who greenlit the way XP does it because XP does it very badly). VXA also has an attack and guard skill so editing those things were a lot more easier. Weapons and Armors have traits which meant diversifying your weapons/armors were easier without scripting. You didn't need to dig through the scripts to edit them. Damage formula was a great upgrade. XP's base damage formula (that you could only edit through scripts) is actually very convoluted. So much so people made guides so people understood how the default damage formula worked, where to find it, and how to edit it.
MV - It's basically everything VXA but better. The only real barrier for some people is Javascript if they have been going from XP - VXA and is thinking on jumping to MV. It has built-in sideview which is a little barebones but has enough flavor that you can easily build off of it rather than starting from barebones. RTP tileset is pretty much like VXA's, its nice.
RTP Battlers is actually better than the previous installations imo as it tones down the 900% contrast that VXA's battlers had and makes more realistic shadows making it personally more pleasing to the eyes.
Their RTP faces and characters are very barebones unlike XP and VXA. It's iconset is absolute garbage imo. Best to just take VXA's RTP iconset and just port it over to MV.
However, its face/sprite/sideview battler generator is easily the best. The creations actually fit into the game unlike VXA where it stares into your soul.
TLDR
XP - Default Anti-Chibi, better default battle system (imo), mapping layers (if you don't pick up MZ), Legacy Support (ruby)
VX - Nothing. Just get XP or VXA.
VXA - The database, legacy support (ruby), sheer number of stuff you get from it's RTP (art-wise)
MV - Side-view, adds onto what was good about VXA except this one has bad RTPs in many areas. Only hurdle being javascript but has a lot of lively support.
